newsitem.title: USA: Zenith, Thomson to offer HDTV sets in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Zenith, Thomson to offer HDTV sets in 1998.

text.p: Zenith Electronics Corp and Thomson Consumer Electronics Inc both announced plans Thursday to introduce high-definition television (HDTV) sets to the consumer market in 1998.

The announcements followed Thursday's decision by the Federal Communications Commission to endorse a single digital television technology standard. The HDTV standard will allow for transmission of one or two high-resolution programs, or up to five analog transmissions, on a single existing channel.
Zenith, along with Thomson a member of the alliance that helped devise the standard, said the launch of its sets will coincide with the lauch of commercial HDTV broadcasts.
A Zenith spokesman was unavailable to comment on how much the HDTV sets will cost once they become available.
Thomson said in a statement the HDTV sets will cost more than today's analog televisions, but was not specific. Company officials were unavailable for further comment.
Zenith and Thomson both manufacture television sets and other consumer electronics products.
Zenith's stock closed up 3/8 Thursday at 10-7/8.
